title: Acid–Base Titration: Finding the Concentration of HCl
summary: Use a burette of 0.125 mol/dm³ sodium hydroxide and phenolphthalein indicator to find the exact concentration of a hydrochloric acid sample, just like a real school laboratory practical.
subject: chemistry
objectives: Work safely with acids and alkalis
Set up, rinse and fill a burette correctly
Identify the end point of a titration with phenolphthalein
Read a burette to ±0.05 cm³ and calculate the titre
Calculate an unknown concentration from the titre

steps.title: Safety first
steps.say: Welcome to the ECH chemistry lab! Sodium hydroxide can damage your eyes, so goggles always come first.

steps.title: Prepare the burette
steps.instruction: Place the funnel in the top of the burette.
hints: Pick up the funnel and drop it on the burette.

steps.title: Prepare the burette
steps.instruction: Rinse the burette with a little sodium hydroxide solution.
steps.say: Rinsing removes water left in the burette, which would dilute the alkali and change your result.
hints: Pour a small amount of NaOH into the burette, then let it drain out.

steps.title: Fill the burette
steps.instruction: Fill the burette with sodium hydroxide to just above the 0.00 cm³ mark, then remove the funnel.
hints: Keep pouring until the liquid is close to the top mark.
Remove the funnel so drips don't change the reading.

steps.title: Initial reading
steps.instruction: Read the burette at the bottom of the meniscus, at eye level, and record the initial reading.
steps.say: Get your eye level with the meniscus to avoid parallax error.

steps.title: Add indicator
steps.instruction: Add 2–3 drops of phenolphthalein to the acid in the conical flask.

steps.title: Position the flask
steps.instruction: Place the conical flask on the white tile under the burette.
steps.say: The white tile makes the first faint pink colour much easier to see.

steps.title: Titrate
steps.instruction: Open the tap and add sodium hydroxide while swirling. Slow down to drop-by-drop near the end, and stop at the first permanent pale pink colour.
hints: Swirl the flask all the time so the solutions mix.
When the pink colour takes longer to disappear, you're close: add one drop at a time.

steps.title: Final reading
steps.instruction: Read and record the final burette reading.

steps.title: Calculate the titre
steps.instruction: Calculate the titre: final reading minus initial reading.

question.prompt: Why does the solution turn pink at the end point?
choices: All the acid has been neutralised and a tiny excess of alkali raises the pH above 8.2
The acid has turned into a base
The temperature of the flask increased
question.explanation: Phenolphthalein is colourless below pH 8.2 and pink above it. One drop of excess NaOH after neutralisation raises the pH sharply.

steps.title: Find the concentration
steps.instruction: Use n = c × V and the 1:1 ratio in HCl + NaOH → NaCl + H₂O to calculate the concentration of the acid in mol/dm³.
steps.say: Moles of NaOH = 0.125 × titre ÷ 1000. That equals the moles of HCl in 25.0 cm³.

hazards.message: Stop! You are handling sodium hydroxide without goggles.
You overshot the end point: the solution is deep pink. A real chemist would repeat the titration.
